topic: Using std::unique_ptr for Exclusive Resource Ownership
explanation: std::unique_ptr is a smart pointer in C++ that provides exclusive ownership of dynamically allocated objects, ensuring that only one pointer can own the resource at a time. This concept is crucial in real-world programming for managing resources like memory, file handles, or network connections, preventing issues such as double deletion or memory leaks. Best practices include using std::unique_ptr instead of raw pointers to enforce automatic resource cleanup via RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization). A common pitfall is attempting to copy a std::unique_ptr, which is explicitly disabled to maintain exclusivity; instead, use move semantics to transfer ownership. In practical scenarios, this pattern is ideal for functions that return dynamically allocated objects or in classes where an object should have a single owner, promoting safer and more idiomatic C++ code.
